gallery.caption: Mix, knead, rise, bake, cool.
gallery.title: The five stages of a loaf

objectives: Name the four things bread is made from.
Explain how yeast makes bread rise.
Follow the steps from dough to baked loaf.
Tell one kind of bread from another.
Bake a small loaf with a grown-up.
Say why bread is good to eat.

sections.body:
Bread is one of the oldest foods in the world. People have been baking it for thousands of years. Today, most bread is made in a big bakery, but the idea is still very simple.

Bread needs only **four** things. The first is **flour**. Flour is made by grinding wheat. The second is **water**. The third is **yeast**. Yeast is a tiny living thing, so tiny you cannot see it. It eats the flour and makes tiny bubbles of gas. The fourth is **salt**. Salt makes the bread taste right.

A baker mixes these four things together. The mix is called **dough**. Dough is soft and sticky. The baker kneads it, which means pushing and folding it with their hands. Kneading helps the bubbles grow evenly.

Then the dough must rest. This time is called **proving**, or rising. The yeast wakes up, eats the flour, and lets out gas. The gas pushes the dough up. The dough grows fat and round.

Now the baker heats the oven. The dough goes in. The heat makes the outside brown and crisp. It also sets the bubbles, so the holes stay for good. The bread is golden and smells warm.

At last the baker takes the bread out and lets it cool. Warm bread is soft inside. Cooled bread keeps its shape and can be cut without squashing.

So a plain loaf is only four ingredients and five steps. That is the whole secret.
examples: Bread is made from flour, water, yeast and salt.
The baker mixes the ingredients into dough.
The dough rises because the yeast makes gas.
sections.heading: What bread is made of

sections.body:
A loaf of bread looks simple, but the holes inside are doing real work.

The holes are made by yeast. Yeast is a fungus, and it eats sugar in the flour. When it eats, it makes two things: gas and alcohol. The gas goes into the dough and puffs it up. The heat in the oven makes the gas expand, so the holes grow bigger. That is why bread is soft inside and never heavy like a stone.

Bread is good food because it is **filling**. It gives you energy for a long afternoon. The flour carries **carbohydrate**, which is the fuel your body uses for running and thinking.

**Wholemeal bread** keeps more of the wheat grain. It has **fibre** in it. Fibre helps your tummy work well. It also fills you up for longer.

**White bread** has more of the grain's flour taken out. It is soft and light. It is fine to eat, but it has less fibre than wholemeal bread.

Bread also carries iron and B vitamins. These help your body carry oxygen around and keep your energy up.

One slice of bread is small, but it is a good thing to eat. Have it with fruit, cheese or eggs, and you get a proper meal.
examples: The holes in bread are made by the yeast.
Wholemeal bread has more fibre in it.
I had a slice of bread with an egg for breakfast.
sections.heading: Why bread rises and why it is good for you

sections.body:
The same four ingredients make very different breads. Here are some you can find.

**White bread** is soft and pale. It is the kind most families buy every day.

**Wholemeal bread** is brown and tastes nuttier. It keeps more of the grain, so it has more fibre.

**Sourdough bread** uses a starter instead of bought yeast. The starter is a lump of dough kept alive for months. Sourdough tastes sour, and it keeps for much longer than other bread.

**Flatbread** is thin and is cooked on a hot flat pan or over a fire. Tortillas, chapatis and lavash are all flatbreads. They do not need an oven.

**Baguettes** are long and thin with a crunchy crust. They come from France and are very popular in Vietnam too, called bánh mì.

**Focaccia** is a flat bread with olive oil and salt on top. It is soft in the middle and crisp at the edges.

The shape and the crust change, but the four ingredients stay the same.
examples: This is sourdough, so it tastes a bit sour.
In Vietnam we eat bánh mì every day.
We baked flatbread on the pan for dinner.
sections.heading: Kinds of bread around the world

sections.body:
These are the words bakers use. Learn them and you can talk about bread like a baker.

**Flour** is wheat grain ground into a fine powder. It is the body of the bread.

**Yeast** is a tiny living fungus that eats sugar and makes gas. It is what makes the dough rise.

**Dough** is the soft sticky mix before it is baked.

**Kneading** is pushing and folding the dough to make it smooth and strong.

**Proving** is the resting time when the dough grows. British bakers call it proving. Some people say rising instead.

**Gluten** is the stretchy part of flour that holds the bread together. When you knead, the gluten wakes up and becomes strong.
examples: Yeast is so small that you cannot see it.
The dough is resting, so it is proving.
sections.heading: The bread words, one by one

terms.example: Flour is made from wheat at the mill.
terms.gloss: Wheat grain ground into a fine powder. It is the main part of the bread.

terms.example: We woke up the yeast in warm water for ten minutes.
terms.gloss: A tiny living fungus that eats sugar in the flour and makes gas.

terms.example: I put the dough in a bowl and covered it.
terms.gloss: The soft, sticky mix of flour and water before it is baked.

terms.example: Kneading the dough for five minutes feels strange at first.
terms.gloss: Pushing and folding the dough so it becomes smooth and strong.

terms.example: The dough is proving now, so it will be ready in an hour.
terms.gloss: The resting time when the dough grows bigger because of the yeast.

sections.body:
This is a simple recipe you can make with a grown-up. It makes one small loaf. Wash your hands first and put an apron on.

You need 300 g of flour, 180 ml of warm water, 1 teaspoon of yeast, 1 teaspoon of salt, and a little oil for the tin. The warm water should feel warm, not hot. Too hot water kills the yeast, and then the dough will never rise.
examples: First I mix the flour, the yeast and the salt.
Now I knead the dough for five minutes.
The dough is twice as big, so it is ready to bake.
sections.heading: How to bake a small loaf at home
steps: Mix the flour, the yeast and the salt in a big bowl.
Pour in the warm water and stir until it is a sticky dough.
Knead the dough on a clean table for 5 minutes.
Cover the bowl and leave the dough to prove for about 1 hour, until it is twice as big.
Oil a tin, put the dough in it, and bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes.
Take the loaf out and let it cool before you cut it.

sections.body:
The oven is the only dangerous part of baking, so let a grown-up handle it. The oven and the tin are hotter than the kettle. Do not touch them. Keep your hair tied back, and keep water away from the hot oven. If the smoke alarm goes off, step away and tell an adult.

Now try these sentences. They work at home, at school, or in a bakery.

If someone asks what is in bread, you can give the whole answer: flour, water, yeast and salt, and nothing else. That is a very good answer.

If you are out of yeast, you can say that the bread will not rise without it. And if the dough does not grow, the yeast was too old, or the water was too hot.
examples: Bread is made of flour, water, yeast and salt.
The oven is hot, so a grown-up should take the tin out.
If the dough does not rise, the yeast is too old.
I kneaded the dough and now it is proving.
sections.heading: Baking safely and saying it out loud

item.summary: Bread is flour and water and a tiny yeast. After reading this you can name the four ingredients, explain why bread rises, bake a simple loaf at home, and tell the difference between kinds of bread.
item.title: How Bread Is Made
